pamphlet_excerpts: Orienteering Physically: Orienteering is a physically demanding activity that takesplace over several kilometers of very mixed and often ruggedterrain.
Hot Weather Result: Hot weather may result in sunburn, heatstroke, heatexhaustion, and dehydration, while cold weather can lead to hypothermia and dehydration.
Hurry Youmight Stumble: In the hurry to be first, youmight stumble onto dangerous animals or poisonous plants.
Spend Fewminutes: Before going out, spend a fewminutes reviewingpossible injuriesand their treatment.
step_by_step_procedure: Thing Prevent Injury: The best thing you can do to prevent injury is to be well-rested, well-fed, and physically fit before going out on an orienteeringcourse.
Normal Night Sleep: A normal night’s sleep and healthy meals will helpyou endure the rigors of the course and decrease the possibilityof a physical or mental slip.
Particularly Vulnerableto: If you are not physically fit, you may be particularly vulnerableto heat.
Dehydration Caused Lack: Dehydration is caused by lack of water in the body.

pamphlet_excerpts: Topographic Map Maps: Using a Topographic Map. maps you will find a number on it that tells its elevation abovesea level.
Orienteering Maps Index: On orienteering maps, the index contour line does nothave an elevation number, but is thicker than the others and isused as a guide for the eye.
Shape Terrain Profileof: You can also “see” the shape of the terrain from the profileof the lines on the paper.
Mountain Perfectly: If a mountain is perfectly conicallike a wizard’s hat, the contour lines depicting the mountainwill look like a bull’s-eye.
step_by_step_procedure: Contour Line: Each contour line will be perfectlycircular, and all will be the same distance apart.
Part Mountain Contour: At one part of the mountain, the contour line may intersect a valley or a depression.
Thecontour Line Ran: If thecontour line ran into the valley, it would lose elevation andwould no longer be considered the same contour line.
Higher Point Ridge: When a higher point like a ridge is encountered, the contour line will “V” downward.

pamphlet_excerpts: Rotate Bezel Orienting: Rotate the bezel until the orienting arrow or north-southlines lie parallel to and in the same direction as the magneticnorth-south lines on the map.
Read Bearing: Read the bearing directlyopposite of the bearing index.
Magnetic North-south Lines: If the magnetic north-south lines are not drawn on themap, convert the language of the compass to that of the map.
Add Number Degrees: Always add the number of degrees of error for west declinationand subtract for east declination.
step_by_step_procedure: Bearing Degrees Points: The bearing is 244 degrees from “A” to “B.” (Points “A” and “B” can be seen in the top photo on page 21.).
Thumb Compassrides Thumb: The thumb compassrides on the thumb andsimplifies map orientationand direction finding while you are on the move.
Itsuffers Bit Accuracy: Itsuffers a bit in accuracy, however, especially in thehands of a novice.
Bearing Index: The bearing index and direction-of-travel arrow are located onthe baseplate.

Begin Giveyou Ideas: This will begin to giveyou ideas about how and where you can lay out the course.
step_by_step_procedure: Few Minutes Reconnaissance: Take a few minutes after your reconnaissance (inspection) of the area to plot a rough course in your notebook.
Willmodify Fine-tune Working: You willmodify and fine-tune this working model of your course whenyou return to map the area.

pamphlet_excerpts: Creating Map Scratch: Creating a map from scratch requires a little preliminaryscouting of the area.
Half-day Thoroughly: Take a half-day to thoroughly familiarizeyourself with things such as the terrain, vegetation, naturaland artificial features, hazards, and potential.
Small Notebook Along: Take a small notebook along to record information aboutthe site that you want to remember as you make your map.
Begin Giveyou Ideas: This will begin to giveyou ideas about how and where you can lay out the course.
step_by_step_procedure: Few Minutes Reconnaissance: Take a few minutes after your reconnaissance (inspection) of the area to plot a rough course in your notebook.
Willmodify Fine-tune Working: You willmodify and fine-tune this working model of your course whenyou return to map the area.
Plan Course Youwill: Unless you plan your course, youwill waste time mapping areas that the course does not use.
Little Bit Planning: This little bit of planning allows you to show up at thestart point, ready to map.

pamphlet_excerpts: Orienteering USA Ruling: Orienteering USA is the ruling body for sanctioned orienteering eventsin the United States.
Its Rule Book: Its rule book is comprehensive and addresses thetechnicalities of holding an event, as well as conduct that is expected ofthe participants.
Few General Rules: A few general rules are provided below, but for detailed information, it is best to consult the rule book or to contact the OUSA. 1.
Competitors Prior Knowledge: Competitors who have prior knowledge of the course that will givethem an unfair advantage should not participate.
step_by_step_procedure: Investigation Ofthe Course: Investigation ofthe course before an event is forbidden. 2.
Navigational Aid Than: The use of any navigational aid other than a compass is prohibited fornavigation during a race.
Includes GPS Global: This includes GPS (global positioning system) units, altimeters, and mobile mapping apps.
Note on post-raceanalysis: Many modern orienteers wear GPS watches solely to recordtheir track for later study.

pamphlet_excerpts: Obscure handrails Ridge Lines: More obscurehandrails might be ridge lines, valleys, tree lines, forest fireburns, or avalanche scars.
Beginners Courses Rely: Beginners’ courses rely heavily on handrails to help thenovice get to each control.
Route Easiest Coursesmay: The route for the easiest coursesmay actually go right down a trail or road, the handrail.
Collecting Check-Off: Collecting, Check-Off, and Catching Features Always look around and take note of the features you passas you move toward the next control.
step_by_step_procedure: There Someobvious Features: There may be someobvious features along the route, such as a large pond or smalllake, that will help send you in the right direction.
Arecollecting Features Lie: These arecollecting features, which lie between you and the control.
Equally But Less: Equally important but less obvious are check-off features, which you will see along the way.
Constantly Verifyyour: You can constantly verifyyour position by making a mental note as you pass the featuresand moving your thumb along the map as you go.
